ReferenceError.explanation: JavaScript reached a name it has never seen. Every name must be created before it is used - with let, const, function, or an import.
ReferenceError.cause: A spelling mistake, or using a let/const variable on a line that runs before the line that declares it.

TypeError.explanation: You did something to a value that does not support it - reading a property of undefined, or calling something that is not a function.
TypeError.cause: Almost always a value that is undefined or null when you expected an object. Something earlier returned nothing.
TypeError.example:
const user = users.find(u => u.id === 9);   // no match, so undefined
console.log(user.name);                    // undefined has no .name
console.log(user?.name);                   // ?. gives undefined instead of failing

SyntaxError.explanation: JavaScript could not understand the shape of your code and stopped before running any of it. Nothing in the file ran.
SyntaxError.cause: An unclosed bracket, brace or quote, or a missing comma in an object or array. Check the line above the one named - an unclosed bracket is only noticed later.

RangeError.explanation: A value was outside the range that operation allows.
RangeError.cause: Most often infinite recursion, or creating an array with a negative or absurd length.

RangeError: Maximum call stack size exce.explanation: A function called itself over and over until JavaScript ran out of room to remember the calls.
RangeError: Maximum call stack size exce.cause: A recursive function whose stopping condition is missing or never reached.
RangeError: Maximum call stack size exce.example:
function count(n) { return count(n - 1); }        // never stops
function countOk(n) { return n <= 0 ? 0 : countOk(n - 1); }

SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON inpu.explanation: JSON.parse was given text that stops in the middle - most often an empty string.
SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON inpu.cause: Parsing a response or a file that turned out to be empty.
SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON inpu.example:
JSON.parse("");        // nothing to parse
JSON.parse("{}");      // an empty object is valid JSON

SyntaxError: Unexpected token.explanation: JavaScript found a character where that character cannot appear. The named token is where it noticed, which is often just after the real mistake.
SyntaxError: Unexpected token.cause: A missing comma or bracket, or JSON.parse being handed something that is not JSON at all.
SyntaxError: Unexpected token.example:
const person = { name: "Ada" age: 36 };   // comma missing
const person = { name: "Ada", age: 36 };

Error.explanation: The program stopped because something threw a general failure. The message after the colon is written by whoever threw it, and is the useful part.
Error.cause: Code that checked a condition and gave up deliberately, or a library reporting a problem.

EvalError.explanation: Something went wrong inside eval(). Modern JavaScript almost never produces this.
EvalError.cause: Using eval at all, which is very rarely the right tool.
EvalError.example:
eval("2 +");        // not complete code
// Prefer a real function to eval - it is easier to read and safer.

URIError.explanation: A URL encoding or decoding function was given text it cannot handle.
URIError.cause: decodeURIComponent on text containing a stray % that is not part of an escape.
URIError.example:
decodeURIComponent("100%");     // % must be followed by two hex digits
decodeURIComponent("100%25");   // %25 is an encoded %

ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND.explanation: The file or package you imported could not be found.
ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND.cause: A path that does not match a real file - in modules the extension is required - or a package that is not available in this sandbox.
ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND.example:
import { add } from "./math";        // no extension
import { add } from "./math.mjs";    // this resolves

ERR_REQUIRE_ESM.explanation: require() was used to load a file that is written as an ES module. The two module systems cannot be mixed that way.
ERR_REQUIRE_ESM.cause: Copying require() from an older example into a project that uses import/export.
ERR_REQUIRE_ESM.example:
const math = require("./math.mjs");   // not allowed for an ES module
import * as math from "./math.mjs";   // use import instead

ERR_UNSUPPORTED_DIR_IMPORT.explanation: You imported a folder. An ES module import has to name a file.
ERR_UNSUPPORTED_DIR_IMPORT.cause: Importing "./utils" and expecting it to find "./utils/index.mjs" the way older code did.
ERR_UNSUPPORTED_DIR_IMPORT.example:
import helpers from "./utils";             // a folder
import helpers from "./utils/index.mjs";   // name the file

EACCES.explanation: The program tried to read or write a file it is not allowed to touch. Programs here may only use files inside their own project.
EACCES.cause: A path leading outside the project, such as one starting with / or containing ..

ENOENT.explanation: The file was not found. The program looked for it and nothing was there.
ENOENT.cause: The file is not in the project yet, or the name does not match exactly, including capital letters.
